title: Committed Serve Charter: escrow credits, quantized windows, and throttling harmonics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers buying Dedicated capacity need a single, unambiguous contractual artifact that defines (a) how committed throughput is measured, (b) how shortfalls are converted into credits, and (c) how autoscaling and throttling interact with entitlements during transient capacity events. Current SLA drafts scatter language between legal, billing, and runtime playbooks leading to inconsistent customer expectations and support flows.

Goal: Produce a single completed SLA & playbook draft that can be embedded into contracts and referenced by onboarding docs. The artifact must: (1) define measurement windows and quantization (tokens-per-minute, 1-minute sampling, 5-minute rolling aggregation, and monthly accounting), (2) standardize the error budget math into a token-minute shortfall model, (3) specify a graduated remediation ladder (notice -> provisional escrow credits -> permanent credit), and (4) document the autoscale interlock and throttling harmonics so customers know when we will throttle versus credit.

Scope: This ticket covers product & legal wording for the SLA, measurement spec for telemetry, example credit computations, operational playbook for support/escalation, and compatibility constraints with Dedicated autoscaler (burst vs. steady-state). It excludes pricing changes for reserved capacity and broader marketplace terms.

Outcomes: Deliver a contract-ready SLA annex, a telemetry acceptance test spec for SRE, and a short customer-facing one-pager explaining the credit algorithm and expected behavioral outcomes during degradations.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Aisha: Initial draft outline shared with Legal (Confluence) and SRE. Legal requested clearer separation between 'degradation' (temporary latency/bandwidth) and 'outage' (complete unavailability).

2025-02-18 - Marcus: Worked with Runtime on measurement windows. Runtime prefers 1-minute sampling with 5-minute rolling quantization to avoid crediting micro-blips. SRE wants additional rolling-1hr fallback for billing reconciliation. Adding both to spec.

2025-02-22 - Legal (Nora Iglesias): Proposed terminology changes: use 'Committed Serve Obligation' instead of 'Guaranteed Serve'; add explicit customer notice windows before provisional credits trigger. Also requested examples in plain English.

2025-02-25 - PM review: Trade-off note — shorter windows reduce customer-perceived exposure but increase noise. We settled on primary 5-minute rolling window for SLA measurement and monthly aggregation for crediting. SRE to provide telemetry proof-of-concept dashboard before next review.

2025-02-28 - Engineering (Rajat): Confirmed how autoscale interlock will report on the entitlement graph; runtime will emit 'entitlement_saturation' and 'autoscale_action' events which map to the playbook. Added a requirement for request-level tags so we can show per-customer degradation traces in the console.

2025-03-01 - Aisha: Updated draft with credit formula and examples; routing policy edge cases added (fallback to compatible model variants excluded from credit if customer opted into lower-fidelity tier). Ready for cross-functional review in 48 hours.
acceptance_criteria: A contract-ready SLA annex doc (plain-text legal wording) signed off by Legal and Finance
A telemetry measurement spec that SRE can implement and validate against real traffic
Example credit computations (three scenarios) included and validated by Finance
An ops playbook that maps runtime signals to customer notice and credit actions
Customer-facing one-pager explaining how autoscale interlock and credits behave
measurement_spec: Primary metric: AggTokensPerMin (aggregated tokens served per minute per customer entitlement). Sampling: 1-minute raw samples. Aggregation: 5-minute rolling median used to compute per-window serve-rate. Monthly reconciliation uses sum of 5-minute windows across the billing month. Degradation detection: window considered failed if observed AggTokensPerMin < 95% of committed rate for that 5-minute window. Outage detection: platform-unreachable or error-rate > 10% for 5-minute window. All telemetry must be signed and stored for 13 months for audit and credit disputes.
credit_formula: Token-minute shortfall model: For each failed 5-minute window, compute shortfall = max(0, committed_tokens_per_minute - observed_tokens_per_minute) * 5 (minutes) = token-minutes_shortfall. Monthly shortfall = sum(token-minutes_shortfall over month). Credit = min(monthly_shortfall / (committed_tokens_per_minute * 60 * 24 * days_in_month), 1.0) * monthly_commitment_fee * credit_weight. Example: Customer commits 1M tokens/min; single 5-min window observed 900k tpm => shortfall = (1,000,000 - 900,000) * 5 = 500,000 token-minutes. If monthly aggregated leads to credit fraction 0.02 => apply 2% credit to monthly billing for compute component. Credit caps: provisional escrow credits trigger at 0.5% monthly fraction; permanent credits applied above 2% using a stepped scale. Detailed table included in annex.
autoscale_interlock: Behavior model: 1) Normal: autoscaler scales within dedicated pool under burst policy and no credits apply. 2) Saturation: when entitlement_saturation metric crosses threshold for >10 consecutive minutes and autoscaler cannot provision within configured burst window, mark windows as degraded for SLA. 3) Fallback model variants: if a customer opts into 'compatible-fallback' then traffic may be routed to lower-fidelity variant; such routed tokens are excluded from crediting if routing policy was applied per customer opt-in. 4) Throttling harmonics: to avoid oscillatory credit churn, we require a 15-minute damping period for re-qualification after a credited degradation event. 5) Notice windows: we will notify customers at 5m/30m/2h marks when sustained saturation is detected and before provisional credits apply.
rollout_notes: Start with closed beta for top 10 Dedicated customers to validate measurement and dispute flows
SRE to deploy dashboard and retention pipeline before legal sign-off (see linked_artifacts)
Legal to produce two versions of annex: (1) default commercial SLA, (2) negotiable enterprise addendum with accelerated remediation options
Billing to simulate credits on last 3 months of historical telemetry to sanity check credit exposure
Customer success to prepare FAQ and onboarding script for how autoscale interlock affects their SLAs
